title: Protocol for cryopreservation of red blood cells that controls ice crystal formation by fulvic acid
protocol: Prepare a FA PBS solution at a concentration of 120 mg/mL and adjust the pH to 7.4.
Store the FA PBS solution at 4°C when not in use.
Add 10 μL of FA PBS to the center of a cleaned coverslip.
Cover the FA PBS droplet with another cleaned coverslip to allow for even diffusion and form a sandwich structure.
Do not apply external pressure to prevent sample squeezing out.
Place the double-layer glass sandwiched with FA PBS on the cryostage.
Decrease the temperature of the hermetic cryostage from room temperature to −120°C at various cooling rates at a constant pressure of 1 atm.
Take images of ice crystals after freezing through a digital camera connected to the microscope.
Measure the size of ice crystals by Image J software.
Turn on the micrograph by Image J software.
Set up the corresponding scale.
Measure the length of 200–300 ice crystals.
Order the data of ice crystal sizes from largest to smallest.
Calculate the mean and standard deviation of the first 60 data points.
Prepare FA PBS solution (same as step 1).
Place a piece of clean coverslip on cryostage.
Close the sealing cover of cryostage.
Cooling the temperature of cryostage to −60°C.
Wait for 30 s.
Open the cryostage sealing cover.
Drop 10 μL FA PBS solutions onto the pre-cooled coverslip by splat cooling method.
Close the cryostage sealing cover.
Wait for 30 seconds.
Heat the temperature of cryostage to −8°C at a rate of 5°C min−1 and hold for 45 min.
Photograph the ice flake through a digital camera connected to the microscope.
Measure the ice crystal size by Image J software.
Prepare FA (240 mg mL−1) and Suc (267 mg mL−1, approximately equal molar concentration compared with FA) PBS solutions.
Place the sample on cryostage.
Freeze liquid sample at various cooling rates.
Heat the cryostage at a rate of 5°C min−1.
Capture high-frame video of the heating process by a camera connected to the microscope.
Prepare two hermetic aluminum crucibles with sealing covers.
Add 2 μL of liquid sample to one crucible.
Use the other crucible as the reference.
Seal both aluminum crucibles.
Place them into the DSC instrument sample holder.
Heat the sample from room temperature to 40°C.
Cool down to 30°C rapidly.
Cool down to −60°C at a series of cooling rates.
Wait for 1 minute.
Heat up to 30°C.
Wait for 1 minute.
Repeat steps b through j three times for each sample.
Plot DSC curves and record melting temperatures at different cooling rates.
Calibrate otago nanolite osmometer with Milli-Q water and NaCl solution.
Prepare FA aqueous solution (120 mg mL−1).
Inject a submicroliter volume of sample into a temperature-controlled sample holder full of immersion oil Type B using a microinjector.
Cool the sample holder rapidly to freeze the aqueous solution.
Warm slowly to prevent ice crystals from completely melting.
Find a disk-shaped ice crystal with a diameter of 15 μm.
Prepare FA PBS solution of double desired concentrations.
Obtain the target concentration of FA PBS solution by mixing an equal volume of the prepared FA PBS solution and PBS buffer.
Blend RBCs dispersion with the prepared FA PBS solution in equal volume.
Disinfect the operator, operating environment, and outer walls of the bottle containing RBCs with 75% medical alcohol before each operation.
Carry out all mixing and transfer processes of FA RBCs in a biosafety cabinet level-II to prevent microbial contamination.
Place cryovials on ice packs during the entire process of FA RBC preparation to reduce the possibility of cell hemolysis.
Mix FA and RBC dispersion evenly with a vortex mixer at low speed to prevent mechanical damage to RBCs.
Prepare RBC dispersion of target concentration for control group samples.
Blend RBC dispersion with Milli-Q water of equal volume to prepare 100% hemolytic samples. If necessary, further break down RBCs by ultrasonication.
Blend RBC dispersion with PBS buffer of equal volume, shake gently and mix evenly to prepare 0% hemolytic samples.
Prepare FA PBS solution.
Mix RBCs and FA PBS in cryogenic vials.
Uniform the mixture of FA and RBC by vortex mixer.
Place all samples on ice pack after mixing.
Fix cryogenic vials to foam floating plate.
Transfer fixed samples to a container containing liquid nitrogen.
Cover the lid of the tank containing liquid nitrogen.
Maintain samples in liquid nitrogen for 2.5 h.
Thaw frozen samples in a refrigerator at 4°C.
Alternatively, use a homemade thermostatic water bath at 45°C to thaw samples.
Strictly control the thawing time to prevent damage to RBCs from high temperature.
Mix 40 μL of FA RBCs with 400 μL PBS buffer.
Uniformly mix the FA RBC-PBS mixture using a vortex mixer.
Centrifuge all samples at 275 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C to remove intact cells.
Collect the supernatant.
Transfer the supernatant to 96 well plates.
Measure the absorbance at the wavelength of 415 nm with a microplate reader.
Calculate cell recovery by subtracting the attained hemolysis from 100%.
Measure the number of intact RBCs by blood analyzer.
Prepare sodium azide (NaN3, 0.05%) solution with PBS as solvent.
Mix fresh RBCs and NaN3 solution.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for different time periods.
Clean RBCs.
Dilute calcein-AM using PBS buffer into a concentration of 100 μM as the working solution.
Mix RBCs (400 μL, 5 × 10^5 cells) and calcein-AM (20 μL).
Uniform the mixture of RBCs and calcein-AM by vortex mixer.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C for 45 min in the dark.
Measure the incubated sample immediately by flow cytometer with the FITC channel.
Measure the viability of RBCs after cryopreservation.
Set control group.
Note: Fresh RBCs with/without calcein-AM staining.
